run.question:
Our US prod cluster is having a checkout incident — investigate using
app-262-prod-logs.

report.summary: The log index app-262-prod-logs does contain data for the US prod cluster the question names: its documents carry cluster="production-us-east-1" (3 docs, all level ERROR) alongside cluster="production-eu-west-1" (2 docs, INFO), and all 5 documents in the whole authorized window fall between 2026-11-23T15:30:56Z and 17:00:56Z. In production-us-east-1 the observed failure chain is: payment-service logged an upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms (16:30:56Z); checkout-service logged a failed POST /api/checkout with 'payment provider response timeout after 30s (Stripe-US)' (15:30:56Z) and then 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 44%)' (17:00:56Z). The deepest origin the evidence names is the upstream payment provider stripe-us, not any Kubernetes object I can see. Separately, the only Kubernetes cluster this Run can read identifies itself as opspilot-m1 (kind), not production-us-east-1: its otel-demo checkout and payment pods are running/ready with 0 restarts and logged successful PlaceOrder / 'Transaction complete.' traffic at 17:21-17:30Z, and its flagd fault-injection flags are all defaultVariant "off" — that is evidence about a different cluster and is not used as the cause here. Prometheus and Jaeger returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on every attempt (9 metric calls, 4 trace calls), so no error-rate, latency baseline or trace evidence exists for either cluster, and the reason stripe-us timed out remains unknown; conclusion is therefore partial.

claims.text: The index app-262-prod-logs contains only 5 documents in the authorized window (2026-10-24T17:31:03Z to 2026-11-23T17:31:03Z), spanning 2026-11-23T15:30:56Z to 2026-11-23T17:00:56Z, split by the documents' own cluster field into production-us-east-1 (3 docs, all level ERROR: checkout-service 2, payment-service 1) and production-eu-west-1 (2 docs, both level INFO: checkout-service).
In cluster production-us-east-1, service checkout-service logged level ERROR at 2026-11-23T15:30:56Z: 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (Stripe-US)'.

In cluster production-us-east-1, service payment-service logged level ERROR at 2026-11-23T16:30:56Z: 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms' — the deepest failing dependency named in the evidence.
In cluster production-us-east-1, service checkout-service logged level ERROR at 2026-11-23T17:00:56Z: 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 44%)'.

The same index carries healthy checkout-service entries for a different cluster, production-eu-west-1, at the same minutes as the US errors: INFO 'Healthy: p95 latency 230ms' at 2026-11-23T16:30:56Z and INFO 'Healthy: success rate 99.7%' at 2026-11-23T17:00:56Z. This shows the log pipeline reported another region as healthy at those times; it neither clears nor explains production-us-east-1.

The Kubernetes cluster readable in this Run is not production-us-east-1: its only node reports providerID kind://docker/opspilot-m1 and its Prometheus alerting rules are labelled cluster: opspilot-m1 with opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909, and its only application namespace is otel-demo. No Kubernetes object, pod status, event or ConfigMap for production-us-east-1 was readable.

In cluster opspilot-m1 all 32 pods (including otel-demo checkout-6578865d87-v6flf and payment-6f7bc865d6-wwqnm) are phase Running with ready containers and restartCount 0, created 2026-11-23T14:36Z; there is no crash, eviction or restart to explain a failure there.

In cluster opspilot-m1 the checkout pod logged successful orders at 2026-11-23T17:30:00Z and 17:30:46Z ('[PlaceOrder] ...', 'payment went through (transaction_id: 3d5c5dcb-6a2e-40ae-a15a-001f47ba4fb0)', 'order confirmation email sent ...') and the payment pod logged 'Transaction complete.' for charges between 17:21:53Z and 17:30:46Z; that is separate-cluster evidence of normal checkout flow, not of production-us-east-1.

In cluster opspilot-m1 the fault-injection ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config has every flag at defaultVariant "off", including paymentFailure ('Fail payment service charge requests n%', variants 100%/90%/75%/50%/25%/10%/off) and paymentUnreachable ('Payment service is unavailable', on/off); the payment deployment consumes flags via FLAGD_HOST=flagd FLAGD_PORT=8013 and checkout reaches payment via PAYMENT_ADDR=payment:8080. This describes opspilot-m1 only.

Supported chain for the production-us-east-1 incident: the upstream payment provider call to stripe-us /v1/charges exceeded payment-service's 30s timeout, so payment charges failed, checkout-service's PlaceOrder then failed with 'payment provider response timeout ... (Stripe-US)' and eventually opened a circuit breaker for payment-service at a 44% failure rate. The evidence ties checkout's symptom to payment-service and payment-service's symptom to stripe-us, but nothing in the evidence explains why stripe-us was slow or unreachable.

An injected payment fault (flagd paymentFailure or paymentUnreachable) is a plausible alternative cause for the US prod pattern, because payment-service's charge path is flag-gated in the demo architecture; however, the flag state I could read is opspilot-m1's (all off) and I could not read production-us-east-1's flagd configuration, so this remains unverified rather than excluded for the US cluster.

Check the stripe-us provider's availability/latency and payment-service's client timeout and circuit-breaker settings in production-us-east-1, and read that cluster's flagd configuration to confirm paymentFailure/paymentUnreachable are off before attributing the failure to the provider.

gaps: No Kubernetes access to production-us-east-1: the readable cluster identifies itself as opspilot-m1 (node providerID kind://docker/opspilot-m1, alert labels cluster: opspilot-m1), so pod status, events, restarts and ConfigMaps of the US prod cluster are unknown and no US-prod object can be named.

Prometheus was unreachable for the whole Run: metrics_range_query (2 calls), execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_metric_names (2 calls), get_all_labels (4 calls) and list_prometheus_rules all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no error-rate, request-count or latency series exist for checkout or payment in either cluster, and no latency trend can be asserted (no baseline was obtained).
Jaeger was unreachable: traces_list_services (2 calls) and traces_search (2 calls) returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so call-edge/span error evidence for checkout and payment is missing.
The kube events query across all namespaces for the authorized window returned no_data (0 events), so nothing about object-level events is known.

Error-filtered log queries on cluster opspilot-m1 returned no_data: filter 'err|error|fail|timeout|panic|exception' matched 0 of 482 payment lines and filter 'err|error|fail|timeout|circuit|panic|exception' matched 0 of 723 checkout lines in 2026-11-23T15:00Z-17:31Z. That shows only that those queries matched nothing; it is not proof the pods logged no errors.
Both pods report 'no previous instance' for the previous container stream, so any earlier crash output is unavailable.
The log index holds only 5 documents over the whole 30-day window (7.1kb), so the log record is extremely sparse; absence of further errors in production-us-east-1 is not established.
Root cause of the 30s stripe-us timeout (provider-side outage, network, DNS, throttling) is unknown; nothing in the evidence shows it.
change_history is not integrated, so when any flag, ConfigMap or configuration changed relative to 15:30-17:00Z could not be checked.

The log documents name services 'checkout-service' and 'payment-service', whereas the readable cluster and the trace service list use 'checkout' and 'payment'; whether these denote the same workloads in production-us-east-1 could not be verified.
next_steps: Provide Kubernetes read access to production-us-east-1 (pods, deployments, events, ConfigMaps such as the flagd configuration) to check whether any fault-injection flag or configuration change coincided with 15:30-17:00Z.
Restore Prometheus and Jaeger access for these clusters and re-check checkout PlaceOrder error ratio, payment charge error rate and p95/p99 latency against a pre-incident baseline.
Ask the payments team to confirm stripe-us /v1/charges latency and error status for 2026-11-23T15:00Z-17:00Z, and verify payment-service's 30s client timeout and circuit-breaker thresholds.
Confirm whether the checkout circuit breaker for payment-service recovered after 17:00:56Z; the latest US-prod log entry in the index is that breaker-open line.

Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident.   scheme: https

groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
